data.name: Andorra
data.region: Southern Europe (Pyrenees), not an EU member (monetary agreement, uses EUR)
data.summary: Personal income tax (IRPF) at a maximum 10%. Gains on listed or unlisted shares are exempt unless the seller (with family) held more than 25% in the prior 12 months, and even then exempt after 10 years of ownership; gains on investment fund units are exempt. Dividends from Andorran companies are exempt; foreign dividends are taxed at 10% with credit for foreign withholding (first EUR 3,000 of savings income exempt). No inheritance, gift or wealth tax. Andorran real estate gains fall under a separate real estate capital gains tax (1%-15%); foreign real estate gains are exempt after 10 years.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: IRPF (Llei 5/2014) on worldwide income: general rate 10%, with a 5% effective rate on the EUR 24,000-40,000 band delivered via a credit. Savings income base reduced by a EUR 3,000 allowance.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident if living in Andorra more than 183 days in the calendar year, or if the main centre of economic activities or interests is in Andorra, directly or indirectly. Requires an Andorran residence permit (see residency).

capital_gains.summary: Gains on shares (listed or unlisted, Andorran or foreign) are exempt if the seller, together with related persons and family up to the third degree, did not hold more than 25% of the company in the 12 months before the sale; larger holdings are also exempt if owned for at least 10 years. Gains on units of any collective investment undertaking are exempt. Exemption excluded for shares of companies whose assets are 50%+ Andorran real estate. Taxable gains (e.g. a >25% stake held under 10 years, bonds) are taxed at up to 10%. Foreign real estate gains exempt after 10 years of ownership. Andorran real estate gains are subject to the separate Impost sobre les plusvàlues (1%-15%, rate depending on holding period), not IRPF.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Holding <= 25% (12-month look-back, family aggregated): exempt. >25% held 10+ years: exempt. Funds: exempt. Foreign real estate held 10+ years: exempt. Andorran real estate held over 10 years: not integrated in the IRPF base.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Shares in Andorran property-rich companies (>=50% Andorran real estate) excluded from the exemption.

capital_gains.professional_trader: Exemption applies to transfers of shares regardless of frequency per the guide; trading as a business activity would be business income at 10%.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: 10 years for >25% stakes and for foreign real estate.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Same exemptions for foreign shares and funds.

dividends.summary: Dividends from Andorran-resident companies (and Andorran funds) subject to Andorran corporate tax are exempt. Foreign dividends are taxable at 10% as savings income, with a deduction for international double taxation; the first EUR 3,000 of savings income is exempt. Withholding of 10% applies at Andorran banks by default.

dividends.rate_basis: General IRPF rate 10% on foreign dividends; with typical 15% treaty WHT the credit (capped at Andorran tax) eliminates the Andorran tax, though Andorra has few treaties so non-treaty WHT often applies.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Not researched (dividends paid to non-residents fall under the non-resident income tax).
dividends.treaty_network: Small treaty network (around a dozen, mainly European: France, Spain, Portugal, Luxembourg, UAE etc.); no treaty with the US (count and list not verified).

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no levy on financial assets. Communes levy small property-related taxes; a vacant-dwelling tax of EUR 5.05/m2 applies to homes empty over 2 years.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Communal property tax (low); vacant dwellings tax EUR 5.05/m2. Property transfer tax (ITP) 4% on purchases.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance or gift tax. Inheritances and donations are outside the IRPF; gains revealed on transfer at death are exempt; gifts of real estate between relatives up to the third degree are exempt from the real estate capital gains tax, and transfers of shares among relatives up to the third degree are exempt from the 4% ITP.

income.name: Andorra

income_tax.summary: IRPF is a flat 10% on the general base after a EUR 24,000 personal minimum, minus a bonus of 50% of the tax on that base capped at EUR 800, so the effective marginal rates are 0% to EUR 24,000, 5% from EUR 24,000 to 40,000 and 10% above. Employees pay 6.5% CASS (pensions 3.5% + general 3%); the self-employed 22% of a chosen base, ceiling EUR 3,674.72 a month.

employment_deduction.note: Deemed 'other expenses' of 3% of gross wages, maximum EUR 2,500 (Govern d'Andorra IRPF guide, section 6.2).

source.title: Impost sobre la renda de les persones fisiques (IRPF) - e-tramits

income_tax.self_employed_notes: CASS self-employed: 22% (10% general branch + 12% pensions) of a chosen base set as a share of the previous year's mean monthly salary: 25% (EUR 668.13, EUR 146.99/month, restricted to certain criteria), 50% (EUR 1,568.67), 75% (EUR 2,004.39), 100% (EUR 2,672.52, EUR 587.95/month, the DEFAULT for those who do not qualify for a reduced rate), 125% (EUR 3,340.65) and 137.5% (EUR 3,674.72, EUR 808.44/month, requires higher net income or turnover). The recorded 22% with a cap of 12 x EUR 3,674.72 = EUR 44,096.64 reproduces the TOP tier (EUR 9,701 a year, about 18% of EUR 54k); the default 100% tier would be EUR 7,055 a year, about 13% of EUR 54k. Figures are from the CASS page updated 30 January 2025; 2026 amounts were not found and the CASS site says it is informational only.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No municipal income tax. The 0% and 5% bands model the EUR 24,000 personal minimum and the EUR 800 bonus; the guide is for tax year 2025, the 2026 guide was not opened. Residents with more than 183 days or the centre of economic interests in Andorra are taxed on worldwide income.

regimes.name: Residence for digital nomads (D.3)
regimes.description: Residence authorisation (D.3) for any newcomer, EU or non-EU, whose work requires no fixed geographic location and uses telecommunications and technology (Govern d'Andorra). Conditions: a favourable ruling from the ministry in charge of the economy that the applicant's work is location-independent, admission within the regulatory quota, effective principal residence in Andorra for at least 90 days a calendar year, proof of owned or rented housing meeting minimum standards (or purchase under way), sufficient financial means as set by regulation, and health and disability insurance valid in Andorra. Initial authorisation two years, first renewal two years, second renewal three years, later renewals ten years. The visa itself does not change tax: residents (183 days or centre of economic interests) pay IRPF on worldwide income under the standard schedule. The income threshold and quota are set by regulation and were not found.
regimes.duration_note: 2 + 2 + 3 years, then 10-year renewals (Govern d'Andorra); 7 years counted as the first three periods.

succession.name: Andorra
succession.summary: Andorran law protects children (or parents if there are none) with a reserved quarter of the estate. It is not in the EU. Trusts are not recognised, and only public-interest foundations are allowed. Several points rest on secondary sources only.
succession.reserved_share: About 25 % of the estate, shared among the children or, with no children, the parents (Act 46/2014 on succession; per UINL summary, secondary source).
succession.foreign_law_note: Per a notarial summary, the testator's national law governs the succession, except where close ties to another state exist. Not under the EU Regulation. Not confirmed from the statute.
succession.trust_note: Andorra is not on the HCCH Trusts Convention table, so it is not in force. Advisers report trusts are not recognised in Andorra. Foundations (Law 11/2008) must pursue general-interest or social purposes.
open_questions: Forced share, applicable-law rule and the absence of a trust law come from secondary sources only.
A reported trust law of 2022 could not be confirmed or ruled out.
Andorra statutes were not read at the Official Gazette (bopa.ad).

assumptions: The family becomes tax resident in Andorra (more than 183 days a year, or centre of economic interests; e-tràmits IRPF) and is entitled to a residence permit. The permit route is not a tax regime: a passive-residence permit does not change the IRPF, which is the same for every resident. Investment and deposit thresholds for the passive permit were reported to have been raised in 2026 (to EUR 1m under Llei 2/2026, from EUR 600,000) but were not confirmed on an official source.

Foreign dividends carry the model's 15% withholding. Andorra has few tax treaties and none with the US, so a higher non-treaty withholding (30% on US dividends) is also fully creditable up to the 10% Andorran tax and changes nothing. A foreign dividend with withholding below 10% (for example a UK dividend with no withholding) would leave Andorran tax of 10% less the withholding; the engine's flat 15% hides that case.

The deduction is computed per country (Guia IRPF; Llei 5/2014 art. 48(3) in the 2014 text took all foreign income together), and the check uses a single source country for simplicity; with several countries the deduction is capped country by country and a low-withholding country would leave some tax.

Realised gains are on listed shares and units of collective investment undertakings held in diversified positions under 25% of each company. Interest and gains on bonds are savings income taxed at 10% and are not covered by the checks, which model equity gains only.

The EUR 5m home: Andorran real estate sold within the transfer-tax rules bears the separate plusvalua tax (1%-15% by holding period), not IRPF; ongoing property taxes are communal and small and are not modelled. Purchase tax (ITP 4%) is a one-off cost outside the projection.
open_questions: Structures considered and not modelled: (1) an Andorran holding company under the special regime for holding companies (Llei 95/2010 art. 38): dividends and gains on participations are exempt from corporate tax, distributions to an individual shareholder are exempt from IRPF when paid by an Andorran company subject to corporate tax, but the general exemption needs a 5% stake held for a year (art. 20) and art. 38 itself states no threshold; whether a portfolio of small listed positions qualifies was not settled, and interest and any non-qualifying income would bear 10% corporate tax (art. 41). Personally the family already pays no Andorran tax on dividends after the foreign-tax deduction and no tax on gains, so a company can only add running costs (about EUR 5,500 to 6,500 a year in a consultancy price list, minimum capital EUR 3,000) and needs real substance in Andorra to avoid being treated as resident elsewhere (Andorra Inc). (2) A private foundation under Llei 11/2008: the foundation law is for general-interest purposes and was not found to allow a family-benefit foundation; not opened. (3) A trust: no Andorran trust law was found.
Whether distributions of a holding-regime company are exempt from the shareholder's IRPF under art. 5 j (company 'subject to' corporate tax even though its income is exempt) was not confirmed.

Transfer tax (ITP) on Andorran real estate passing by inheritance: a secondary source says transfers on death are outside the transfer tax and exempt from the foreign-investment tax, but the statute was not opened. The existing tax-file question stays open.

Llei 5/2014 is read in its 2014 BOPA text (art. numbers) and the 2025 Govern guide; later amendments (including Llei 5/2023 on direct taxation) were not compared line by line, but the guide confirms the 10% rate, the EUR 3,000 minimum, the 25% and 10-year exemption and the deduction.
Passive residence: confirm the current investment and deposit amounts on govern.ad (reported change in 2026).

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary IRPF residence)
paths.note: Foreign dividends are savings income taxed at the flat 10% IRPF (Llei 5/2014 art. 43) after a EUR 3,000 allowance (art. 37), but the 15% foreign withholding is deducted from the Andorran tax, up to that tax (art. 48), so no Andorran tax is left on them. Gains on shares are exempt when the holder with relatives up to the third degree never exceeded 25% of the company in the previous 12 months (art. 5 k), which a diversified portfolio meets. No wealth tax, no inheritance or gift tax.

immigration.name: Andorra
immigration.summary: Andorra is outside the EU and EU citizens have no free movement there: everyone needs a permit. The main route for people who do not work is passive residence, which since Law 2/2026 requires an investment of EUR 1,000,000 in Andorran assets (or EUR 800,000 in a home) plus a non-refundable EUR 50,000 payment, and 90 days a year in Andorra. Working and self-employed permits are quota-limited.
immigration.naturalisation: Reported 20 years of continuous residence for ordinary naturalisation (earlier research, not re-verified this session).
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Andorran nationality generally requires renouncing the previous nationality (not re-verified this session).

routes.name: Passive residence (residència sense activitat lucrativa)
routes.summary: A residence permit without the right to work, for people who invest EUR 1,000,000 in Andorran assets or buy a home, pay a non-refundable EUR 50,000 and spend at least 90 days a year in Andorra.
routes.requirements: As reported for Law 2/2026 (in force 13 February 2026 per Andorra Insiders; approved by the Consell General on 22 January 2026): invest at least EUR 1,000,000 in Andorran assets (financial instruments, debt, funds, stakes in local companies; raised from EUR 600,000), or buy one residential property worth at least EUR 800,000 (raised from EUR 600,000), or, as reported, contribute EUR 400,000 to the state Housing Fund; non-refundable payment to the Andorran Financial Authority (AFA) of EUR 50,000 for the main applicant and EUR 12,000 per dependent (previously a refundable deposit); health insurance; clean record; no work in Andorra. Applications filed before the law took effect are processed under the old rules.
routes.investment_options: EUR 1,000,000 in Andorran assets; or EUR 800,000 in one residential property; reported alternative of EUR 400,000 to the Housing Fund (not confirmed from the law text).
routes.fees_note: Non-refundable AFA payment, EUR 12,000 per dependent. An immigration fee of EUR 2,500 (EUR 500 per dependent) is reported by one source only.
routes.physical_presence: At least 90 days a year in Andorra
routes.family: Spouse and dependents included for EUR 12,000 each.
routes.tax_note: Passive residents can become tax resident after 183 days; Andorra income tax is 0% to 10%. A permit alone does not make you tax resident.
